title: Is there now a better trend in youth mental health? - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration's latest National Survey on Drug Use and Health, covering trends from 2021 to 2025, shows continued improvement across youth mental health and substance use metrics: fewer 12-17 year olds reporting tobacco, alcohol, marijuana and binge drinking, fewer substance use disorders, and declining major depressive episodes and suicidality. The survey nearly lapsed after its entire 17-member team was laid off by the Trump administration.

themes.theme: Youth substance use and mental health trends

insights.claim: Adolescents aged 12 to 17 reported lower past-month use of tobacco, alcohol, marijuana and binge drinking, and lower past-year illicit drug and marijuana use, initiation of drinking, vaping or marijuana, and substance, alcohol or drug use disorders.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
entities: National Survey on Drug Use and Health
insights.so_what: Sustained secular decline in youth substance consumption is a structural headwind for tobacco, vaping, alcohol and cannabis demand at the entry cohort.

insights.claim: Adolescents also showed declining trends for major depressive episodes and fewer reported serious thoughts of suicide, making a suicide plan and attempting suicide, over the 2021 to 2025 period.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Cuts against the dominant 'teen mental health crisis worsening' narrative that underpins social-media regulation and teletherapy demand assumptions.

insights.claim: The National Survey on Drug Use and Health nearly lapsed when its entire 17-member team was laid off by the Trump administration, yet SAMHSA still released the latest report with data spanning 2021 to 2025.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
entities: National Survey on Drug Use and Health
insights.so_what: Key federal statistical series are staffing-fragile; continuity risk in official data affects anyone relying on it for health-sector or consumer forecasting.
insights.quote: the entire 17-member team responsible for it was laid off by the Trump administration
insights.locator: There was some uncertainty about the future
